attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the causal claim in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the CUDA explanation and practical dominance claim. The surrounding discussion supplies the AI GPU scope.

contract.note: Entrenched practical dominance sustained materially by CUDA is an ordinary reading. The contract appropriately avoids requiring sole supply, legal monopoly or exclusive causation.

evidence.note: Dated market research describes dominance and competing progress, but covers broader accelerators and does not establish CUDA's causal contribution.
The specified version documents competitive Gaudi performance and software shortcomings. These NPU comparisons do not establish late-2025 GPU ecosystem parity or market dominance.
The authority's 2024 account describes emerging alternatives. It provides historical context, not a measurement of the competitive position at publication.

reviews.rationale: The packet indicates NVIDIA dominance and software advantages, alongside improving alternatives. It lacks sufficiently matched late-2025 market, adoption and switching evidence to establish or defeat the claimed practical monopoly and CUDA mechanism.

attribution.note: The assertions are Zitron's own endorsed statements.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the five contemporary assertions and their categorical language. No explicit condition or forecast deadline is omitted.

contract.note: The readings of task usefulness, comparable-quality productivity and comparable-output inference cost are ordinary interpretations of the firm language. The contract retains population limits and distinguishes customer prices from provider costs.

evidence.note: The randomized study supports slowdown for experienced developers working in familiar repositories with early-2025 tools. It does not establish general developer slowdown.
Measured success on multistep tasks contradicts categorical agent failure. The 50% success threshold also documents substantial reliability limits.
The November version finds declining prices at comparable benchmark performance, opposing the contract's unit-cost reading. It does not measure provider production costs or aggregate spending.

Available before evaluation, but its measurement window extends beyond the target period. Selection problems and intervals including no effect further limit its ability to resolve the historical claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports reliability limitations and developer slowdown in one specified setting. Successful agent tasks contradict categorical failure, and falling comparable-performance prices contradict the unit-cost assertion. General developer slowdown and unreliability across all AI products remain unestablished.

attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts the capacity shortfall; the nearby Nadella quotation is supporting material, not the attributed statement.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the present capacity and power shortfall for the identified Blackwell cohort.

contract.note: Existing compatible, powered capacity is the ordinary reading. The latest completed month is a reasonable reporting approximation, and reconciling shipment units is necessary to assess the actual cohort.

evidence.note: The report conveys Microsoft's own disclosure of facility constraints. It provides no Blackwell-specific inventory or global capacity assessment.
The research establishes regional market tightness in H1 2025, not November worldwide capacity compatible with the shipment cohort.

Published before evaluation, this retrospective analysis questions die-versus-package counting in the October shipment figure. It does not establish available capacity or independently settle the cohort's requirements.

reviews.rationale: Microsoft's bottleneck and regional vacancy data cannot establish a cohort-wide shortfall. The counting-unit analysis weakens unreconciled power arithmetic without proving sufficient capacity. Neither matched electrical requirements nor a sufficiently complete inventory of compatible powered facilities is supplied.

attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses the statement about NVIDIA's market importance.

semantics.note: The normalization faithfully extracts the market-importance assertion. Its metaphor has an ordinary empirical reading and does not assert a future collapse.

contract.note: Unusually large influence on broad indexes fairly operationalizes the metaphor. November weights are appropriately close to publication.

evidence.note: Reuters reports November weights of 8% in the S&P 500 and roughly 10% in the Nasdaq 100, establishing substantial individual influence on both indexes.

reviews.rationale: The dated index weights establish unusually large mechanical influence on major US indexes, satisfying the fair ordinary reading of market importance. No systemic-collapse inference is needed or established.
